decision: The concrete Kiota review obstacles are resolved in a validated local successor; external submission remains human-gated. Select the trust-assumption reporting pilot READY and unstarted because its source/reuse preparation offers the highest-value remaining shared conformance output. Do not extend this owner-requested PR refinement into another research item.

categories.assessment: The Kiota repair and refinement have complete local outputs. The next distinct question is transitive assumption visibility across two supported report paths; this outranks repeating implementation packaging or opening less-specified stateful histories.

The exact malformed signature, downstream evidence, refined patch and direct comparison tests remain reusable. Assumption reporting reuses axiom and checked-object assets; stateful validation needs a supported session contract. No old semantic outcome is reinterpreted.

A dated read-only refresh found Kiota main unchanged and an open maintainer draft with disjoint files; no apparent open duplicate or requested feedback requires another local change. Submission awaits exact human authorization, while other held contributions have no new feedback in this scope.

The pinned Lean reference algorithm and existing supervisor were reused; no new method is claimed. Next work should inspect retained toolchain assumption/reporting contracts before binding the reporting matrix. The stateful alternative needs a separate contract survey.

The selected reporting item can begin its authorized source/reuse and protocol-binding phase locally. Kiota launch and package gates have passed; external submission authority is unavailable but does not block the independent local reporting preparation.

candidates.rationale: READY and unstarted for a source/reuse assessment and staged protocol binding. Existing retained axiom and report tooling supports this preparatory phase; exact fixtures, expected transitive sets and observable paths must be committed before any launch.

The request-history question remains useful but cannot yet be promoted because its supported session boundary and failure-recovery contract are not established; it is less immediately reusable than the assumption-reporting protocol.

blockers.reason: Establish supported public session, termination, rollback, fresh-name and dependency-order contracts before freezing the six request histories.
